  "hypothesis": "Predicted that nonface line patterns with salient Gestalt information would elicit facelike holistic processing in novices, as measured by a congruency effect in an adapted composite task.",
  "design": "within, with conditions varying stimulus type (faces vs. line patterns), alignment (aligned vs. misaligned), congruency (congruent vs. incongruent), and target matching (same vs. different top parts).",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Line-pattern composite stimuli conveying Gestalt information (connectedness, closure, continuity, and emergent features) compared against composite faces, presented in aligned and misaligned configurations.",
  "outcome_measure": "Response sensitivity (d') calculated from same/different judgments on the top parts of composite stimuli.",
  "population_and_setting": "Twenty-two participants tested in a laboratory setting.",
  "sample_size_total": 22,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Twenty-two people registered and participated.",
  "analysis_plan": "A 2 (alignment) x 2 (congruency) x 2 (task) repeated measures analysis of variance (ANOVA), followed by separate repeated measures ANOVAs and paired t-tests for each task condition.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants performed two composite tasks (one with faces, one with line patterns) in counterbalanced order, making same/different judgments on top parts while ignoring bottom parts."
